prompt: A JList named "items" holds five fruits. Complete the selection listener so a JLabel named "choice" always shows the selected fruit, or "nothing" when the selection is empty.
explanation: A JList reports selection changes to ListSelectionListeners; programmatic calls such as setSelectedIndex and clearSelection fire the listener just like mouse clicks would. getSelectedValue() returns the selected element, or null when the selection is empty, so one null check covers both the "picked something" and "picked nothing" cases. Note that the list is wrapped in a JScrollPane -- the tests still find it because they search the component tree recursively by name.
hints: items.getSelectedValue() returns the selected string, or null when nothing is selected.
The listener fires for both selecting and clearing, so one method body handles both cases.
Use a null check: if the value is null show "nothing", otherwise show the value itself.
